Established in 1990, we are now a 700+ member strong global organization with a presence in 22+ countries. For more information about sa.global, please click www.saglobal.com. ROLE PURPOSE This is a newly created, high-visibility leadership role with the mandate to define and scale the future of our global commercial operating model. As Global Head of Revenue Operations & Commercial Excellence, you will bring together strategic ownership of CRM, sales operations, commercial governance, revenue forecasting, Microsoft partner compliance, and incentive management — creating a more connected, data-driven, and scalable approach to growth. You will have the opportunity to shape how a transforming and ambitious organization goes to market, improve commercial discipline, and accelerate sustainable growth. Working closely with the Executive Leadership Team, CFO, and business leaders across the organization, you will establish the processes, insights, and capabilities that enable our commercial teams to perform at their best. This is a unique opportunity to build the foundation of a world-class commercial engine — empowering teams to focus on customers, growth, and long-term success while ensuring the organization operates with clarity, consistency, and excellence. Who Thrives In This Role You are someone who finds satisfaction in making the machine work. You care about data integrity, process consistency, and operational reliability — not because you enjoy bureaucracy, but because you understand that disciplined commercial operations are what allow a sales organization to scale without breaking. You are comfortable operating across multiple stakeholders and geographies without direct authority over most of them. You know how to influence through clarity, structure, and the quality of the data and processes you put in front of people. You do not need to own the strategy to have a significant impact on how it lands in market. You have a strong bias toward automation and efficiency — you actively look for ways to replace manual reporting with system-driven insight and are energized, not threatened, by the opportunity to embed AI into revenue operations workflows. You are pragmatic about change: you know that a new process only works if people adopt it, and you invest the time to make that happen. If you want a role where operational excellence directly enables commercial growth — and where you build the infrastructure that an ambitious, transforming organization runs on — this is the right role for you. Key Accountabilities Sales Operations & CRM Governance: Own the end-to-end sales operations function, including CRM system integrity, pipeline governance, deal stage discipline, and process adherence. Ensure the commercial infrastructure provides a single, reliable source of truth for pipeline, forecasting, and revenue reporting across all entities and verticals. Revenue Forecasting & Commercial Reporting: Own the forecasting cadence, methodology, and accuracy standards. Deliver consolidated revenue forecasts to ExCo and the CFO, ensuring alignment between pipeline data, financial targets, and capacity planning. Surface risks, gaps, and trends early enough to enable intervention. Pricing, Discount Governance & Commercial Compliance: Own the group pricing framework, discount approval processes, and commercial contract review from an operational standpoint. Ensure deal pricing and margin modelling follow established guardrails and that intercompany pricing rules are applied consistently across multi-entity deals. Microsoft Partner Desk & Programme Compliance: Own the operational relationship with Microsoft’s partner programmes, including partner solutions designations (MPD), co-sell registration processes, incentive tracking, and certification maintenance. Ensure sa.global meets all programme requirements and captures available benefits. Incentive Calculation & Commission Administration: Own the end-to-end process for calculating, validating, and administering sales incentives and variable compensation. Ensure accuracy, transparency, and timely delivery in close collaboration with Finance and the CPO. Pursuit Management & Sales Process Governance: Own pursuit management standards, including stage entry and exit criteria, deal review cadences, go/no-go qualification, and readiness-to-sell approval processes. Drive adoption of consistent sales methodology across all markets. Technology Landscape & IT Liaison: Own the commercial technology stack in partnership with IT, including CRM configuration, sales tooling, reporting platforms, and data quality governance. Define business requirements, drive adoption, and ensure systems evolve to support AI-enabled and automated revenue workflows. GTM Enablement Coordination: Ensure GTM enablement materials, playbooks, and training produced by the Transformation Programme Lead are operationalized into the sales motion. Own readiness-to-selling processes and demand-to-pipeline alignment between Marketing and Sales. Win/Loss Analysis & Continuous Improvement: Lead structured win/loss analysis and embed learnings into repeatable sales plays. Scale what works by industrializing successful pursuits into standardized, replicable commercial motions. Key Outcomes — What Success Looks Like Forecast accuracy is consistently within agreed tolerance, and ExCo has a dependable forward view of revenue across verticals and geographies without needing to chase data. CRM is trusted as the single source of truth: pipeline data is clean, deal stages are meaningful, and reporting is automated rather than manually assembled. Microsoft partner programme requirements are met proactively, incentives are fully captured, and partner desk interactions are structured and timely. Incentive calculations are accurate, auditable, and delivered on schedule — removing a recurring source of friction between Sales, Finance, and HR. Commercial governance (pricing, discounting, contract review) operates as a reliable, scalable system rather than ad hoc escalation — with AI-assisted tooling progressively reducing manual effort in deal modelling and compliance checks. Core Skills Skills Level Definition Revenue Operations & Sales Process Design - Ability to design, implement, and govern end-to-end sales operations processes across a multi-country, multi-vertical commercial organization. CRM & Commercial Systems Management - Deep hands-on expertise in CRM platforms (Dynamics 365 preferred), reporting infrastructure, data quality governance, and sales tooling architecture. Financial Acumen & Forecasting - Strong understanding of revenue forecasting, pipeline analytics, margin modelling, and the linkage between commercial activity and financial outcomes. Commercial Governance & Compliance - Ability to design and enforce pricing frameworks, discount governance, and contract review processes with consistency and rigor. Microsoft Partner Ecosystem - Working knowledge of Microsoft partner programmes, co-sell mechanics, MPD reporting, incentive structures, and certification requirements. Stakeholder Management & Cross-Functional Coordination - Ability to operate across Finance, IT, Sales, HR, and Marketing without direct authority, aligning operational processes to strategic intent. Data Analysis & Business Intelligence - Ability to translate commercial data into actionable insight through dashboards, win/loss analysis, and pipeline diagnostics. AI-Enabled Process Design - Awareness of how AI and automation can improve revenue operations workflows — including forecasting, deal scoring, CRM hygiene, and incentive modelling — with willingness to adopt and champion new tooling. What We Offer Strategic leadership role with global impact – the opportunity to define and build sa.global’s Revenue Operations and Commercial Excellence function, shaping how a global Microsoft partner scales, operates, and grows. Executive-level exposure and influence – work closely with the Executive Committee, CFO, and senior leaders across Sales, Marketing, Delivery, Finance, and Technology to drive commercial transformation and measurable business impact. Opportunity to build and transform – create scalable processes, governance frameworks, operating models, systems, and insights that become the foundation for predictable growth and commercial excellence. Key role in our AI-enabled transformation journey – help modernize commercial operations through automation, data-driven decision-making, advanced analytics, and innovative approaches to revenue management. Competitive executive compensation package – an attractive base salary, performance-based bonus, and benefits package aligned with the seniority, scope, and strategic impact of the role. Flexible hybrid working model – work from anywhere in Europe while collaborating with global teams across multiple countries and markets. Global and diverse environment – partner with talented colleagues across our international organization and contribute to a truly multicultural and collaborative workplace. High level of ownership and autonomy – the freedom to challenge existing ways of working, introduce improvements, and directly influence how sa.global scales for the future. Professional growth and continuous learning – access to opportunities to expand expertise in revenue operations, AI transformation, commercial excellence, and global leadership. Culture of innovation and accountability – join an environment where initiative is valued, impact is visible, and leaders are empowered to make meaningful change. All information shared as part of your application will be treated with strict confidentiality and handled in accordance with applicable data protection regulations, including GDPR requirements. Candidate information will only be used for the purpose of assessing suitability for this position and managing the recruitment process. Access to candidate data will be limited to the relevant stakeholders involved in the selection process. sa.global is committed to fair and transparent compensation practices. review_candidates.description: WHO ARE WE? Shelter Movers is a national, volunteer-powered charitable organization providing moving and storage services at no cost to individuals and families fleeing abuse. We collaborate with local businesses and community agencies to support people, primarily women and children, as they transition to a life free of violence. Every year, in collaboration with community partners, our volunteer teams contribute tens of thousands of hours across Canada to support people transitioning to lives free of violence and abuse. Working at Shelter Movers means creating a meaningful impact for families experiencing abuse. It also means showing ally-ship and playing a tangible role in breaking the cycle of gender-based violence in Canada. We are growing and looking to add caring, compassionate, competent people to join our team. At Shelter Movers, we know that diverse backgrounds, skills, and life experiences make us stronger and better equipped to understand and serve our diverse client community. We are committed to creating an inclusive environment where everyone feels valued, respected, and empowered to share their unique perspectives in support of our mission. We welcome and encourage applications from individuals of all backgrounds without regard to age, colour, race, sex, religion or belief, national or ethnic origin, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, marital status, family or parental status, genetic characteristics, or physical or mental disability, or any other background that sets you apart, AND who share our passion for making a difference.  PURPOSE OF YOUR ROLE We are seeking a strategic and passionate leader to serve as our next Chief Executive Officer (CEO) to guide the organization into its next phase of growth and impact. Reporting directly to the board of directors, the CEO will provide executive leadership for all aspects of the organizational operations, fund development, public advocacy, financial stewardship and strategic growth.  The ideal candidate has a proven track record leading a successful not-for-profit organization, ideally with national reach and demonstrated commitment to the gender-based violence (GBV) sector. You are able to advocate for the organization with external stakeholders, staff and volunteers to sustain and grow our impact nationally. RESPONSIBILITIES Organizational Leadership and Culture Lead, coach, and support the leadership team to manage a geographically distributed team of staff and volunteers to deliver operational excellence in the communities we serve. Foster a healthy organizational culture rooted in accountability, collaboration, continuous improvement, inclusion, and safety. Ensure appropriate oversight of organizational performance, financial sustainability, compliance, and risk management with accountability to the board. Strategic Leadership & Governance  With the board, establish a strategic plan that creates the framework for delivering on our mission over the next 3-5 years.  Create an annual operating plan and budget, supported by key metrics, to manage and report on organizational performance to the board and stakeholders.  Develop and sustain effective governance practices and maintain strong relationships with the board.  Establish key operating metrics and manage organizational performance against strategic goals and key performance indicators. Proactively manage organizational, operational and financial and reputational risks and recommend appropriate strategies to the board. Fundraising, Philanthropy & Revenue Growth Set the fundraising strategy and cultivate a sustainable philanthropic culture with support from the board, staff, and community partners.  Champion a culture of donor stewardship, accountability, and impact reporting. Support the development and execution of national fundraising campaigns and revenue-generating initiatives. Maintain and nurture meaningful relationships with major donors, corporate partners, foundations, and government funders to expand organizational capacity and impact. External Relations, Advocacy & Public Profile  Serve as the primary representative and spokesperson for Shelter Movers with donors, community partners, government and the media. Build and maintain strong relationships with government officials, sector leaders, corporate executives, media, and community organizations. Increase national awareness of Shelter Movers through strategic communications and thought leadership. Advocate for issues affecting survivors of gender-based violence and strengthen organization’s influence within the sector. Identify opportunities that enhance the organization's reputation, visibility, and strategic partnerships. REQUIRED EXPERIENCE Experience leading successful not-for-profit organizations, particularly with a national reach Proven track record of building and leading high-performing teams of staff and volunteers Demonstrated commitment to work in the GBV sector Experience developing and managing strategic plans with board, staff and stakeholders Proven track record of robust operational and financial management Experience creating fund development strategies and cultivating donor relationships Exceptional fundraising and major gift development experience with a demonstrated history of securing significant philanthropic revenue. Experience developing a network of community partners and supporters to extend impact Executive-level communication and media relations, including public speaking, presentations, media interviews, and storytelling. Outstanding relationship-building abilities with donors, corporate partners, government representatives, foundations, and community leaders. Demonstrated commitment to equity, diversity, inclusion, accessibility, and trauma-informed leadership. ADDITIONAL DETAILS Knowledge of the gender-based violence sector, particularly women's shelters. Advanced understanding of gender studies, including anti-racist, anti-oppressive, and intersectional frameworks affecting survivors of abuse. Existing relationships with philanthropic leaders, corporate executives, foundations, and government funding bodies. Experience engaging with provincial and federal government stakeholders. Experience leading national awareness campaigns or advocacy initiatives. Bilingualism (English/French) is an asset. Willingness to travel nationally as needed (10%). ROLE DETAILS JOB TYPE: Full-Time | Permanent COMPENSATION: $130,000 - $160,000  LOCATION: Canada / Remote HOURS OF WORK: 35 hours per week (with some evening and weekend availability as needed) SOME OF THE EXTRAS Health/Dental Coverage Phone Stipend Employee Assistance Program Discounted fitness membership Parental Top-up Paid time-off Shelter Movers is pleased, and committed to providing an accessible recruitment and selection process in accordance with the Accessibility for Ontarians with Disabilities Act (AODA).
